source.title: Representation of action-specific reward values in the striatum

confidence_rationale: Foundational single-unit primate result: >1/3 of striatal projection neurons were tuned to the value of ONE of the two actions during the pre-choice delay, with fewer tuned to relative value or to the choice itself. This is the direct evidence that ACTION-value (an actor-critic-style action-value signal) is explicitly represented in the striatum, which is what resolves the Rothenhoefer divergence: action-value learning survives a VS lesion because it lives in a different (dorsal/caudate-putamen) striatal population. Confidence 0.66 -- high locus-mapping fidelity for the 'REE's DV is action-like' question, moderated by the correlational (recording, not causal) design and the species/task gap.
failure_signatures: The signal is an ACTION-value code, not an advantage or a baseline per se -- so the paper establishes WHERE an informative action-critic lives but does not itself demonstrate that removing/flattening it produces active degradation; that causal step is imported from lesion (Rothenhoefer) and computational (Fujimoto, Tucker) entries.

Fewer neurons coded relative value or the choice; a substrate that represents absolute action-values without a strong relative/advantage code is consistent with REE's measured pathology (an advantage dominated by variance) but the paper does not measure variance of the value estimate.

mapping.source_claim_statement: During a delay before choosing between left and right handle turns based on estimated reward probabilities, more than one-third of striatal projection neurons were selective to the value of ONE of the two actions; fewer were tuned to relative values or to action choice, indicating explicit representation of action values in the striatum.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-475 characterises the critic on REE's MECH-457 actor-critic pathway. The claim's notes commissioned this lit-pull to decide whether REE's foraging DV is stimulus-like (resource-directed) or action-like. Samejima shows action-specific reward VALUE is a real, explicitly-coded striatal signal -- i.e. the brain implements exactly the action-value critic REE's pathway is trying to learn. This licenses treating REE's DV as action-like and locates the biological analog of REE's critic in the dorsal/caudate-putamen action-value population rather than the VS.
mapping.ree_translation_note: Together with Rothenhoefer 2017 (VS lesion spares action-value learning) this resolves the divergence: action-value learning is intact after a VS lesion because it is carried by this dorsal-striatal action-value code, not the VS.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Correlational single-unit evidence in a two-action handle-turn task, not a causal manipulation and not a foraging environment; it establishes the EXISTENCE and LOCUS of an action-value critic, not that its uninformativeness causes active competence loss. The destructiveness prediction still rests on the lesion and computational entries.
mapping.source_context: Extracellular single-unit recording from striatal projection neurons in monkeys performing a free-choice reward-probability task; regression of delay-period activity onto action values estimated by an RL model.

confidence_components.notes: Canonical Science paper, high source quality. mapping_fidelity 0.7 for the action-vs-stimulus locus question it directly answers; transfer_risk moderate (monkey handle-turn -> REE foraging). Correlational design is why direction is 'supports' at 0.66 rather than higher.
